Data to generate these charts can be found in the “VehicleCount” and “SpeedOperationTimeHours” columns of the files labeled “AvgSpeedAndCIsBrokenOutByHourID_vocation_fdna.csv”; these results files are further explained in Section 5.3: Average Speed, which uses the same level of aggregation as this data density section. 4.2 CE-CERT Data Density We now examine the available data for the CE-CERT data set. Similar to FleetDNA, there tend to be less-robust data from rural roads and on weekends than on urban roads or weekdays. Figure 7 displays the data available for combination-unit short-haul vehicles from the CE-CERT database. CERT only has less than 1 hour of data per hour ID, and this category will be excluded from further analysis (shaded gray). In contrast, rural freeways have up to 30 hours of data in the afternoon, albeit with some spotty hourly coverage in mornings and evenings, and results will be interpreted with caution (shaded yellow). Urban roads have robust data, with 35 vehicles and hundreds of hours of data on weekdays. About 15–20 of those vehicles operated on weekends. With upward of 20 vehicles recorded and over 30 hours of data at times, results from urban other roads can be interpreted with some confidence going forward. With fewer vehicles and about half the hours recorded, some care should be taken when interpreting urban freeway results (shaded yellow). Figure 7.
